problem_text:
A logistics manager is selecting cargo containers to load onto a freight truck. Available containers are:
* Container 1: weight 30kg, value $190
* Container 2: weight 29kg, value $84
* Container 3: weight 50kg, value $256
* Container 4: weight 24kg, value $42
* Container 5: weight 17kg, value $299
* Container 6: weight 14kg, value $79
* Container 7: weight 43kg, value $279
* Container 8: weight 19kg, value $51
* Container 9: weight 12kg, value $12
* Container 10: weight 36kg, value $285
* Container 11: weight 30kg, value $294
* Container 12: weight 31kg, value $152
* Container 13: weight 12kg, value $12
* Container 14: weight 42kg, value $232
* Container 15: weight 23kg, value $164
* Container 16: weight 28kg, value $34
* Container 17: weight 45kg, value $26
* Container 18: weight 3kg, value $137
* Container 19: weight 28kg, value $56
* Container 20: weight 3kg, value $202
* Container 21: weight 31kg, value $117
* Container 22: weight 8kg, value $146
* Container 23: weight 2kg, value $98
* Container 24: weight 31kg, value $34
* Container 25: weight 5kg, value $19

The truck has a maximum payload capacity of 417 kg. Determine which containers to load to maximize the total value without exceeding this weight limit. Each container must be loaded entirely or left behind.
